why: SPEC E2-C 11.4. The second round's matrix must be frozen BEFORE its own D0, and the first round was bitten by the opposite order: 27 cells used a gesture the product never uses and the matrix had not said anything about it. This file is the draft; it becomes the matrix when the v3 hashes exist and `status` is set to `frozen-before-D0`.

steps: fill the five baseline hashes from dist/profiles/e2-editor-v3 and the CURRENT shell bundle generation (v4 as of 2026-08-16; check tools/build_e2_c_shell_bundle.py's MANIFEST rather than hard-coding a number)
record the freeze in SPEC E2-C's revision table
freezeProcedure.entryAssertion: D0 must refuse to run while any baseline hash is still 'TO-BE-FILLED-AT-RELINK' or while status is not 'frozen-before-D0'. Without this the window between the relink and the freeze has no guard, which external review named on 2026-08-16 as the one place the first round's mistake could repeat.
freezeProcedure.entryAssertionImplementedBy: tools/e2_c_matrix_entry.py (assert_entry/require_entry), called by tools/run_e2_c_d0.py before a browser starts and by tools/analyze_e2_c_d0.py before a verdict is written. Wired into `make test-e2-c-static` with a 7-check self-test. Written 2026-08-16: the assertion existed as this paragraph for a day, and a paragraph does not refuse to run a round.

baseline.whyFive: SPEC E2-C 11.3. The first round bound four. This round changes semantics that live in sdk-manifest.json itself -- abiVersion, limits, gestures, and the gesture mask the engine pushes in at init -- so the manifest's own sha256 is the fifth identity. Finding 045 already recorded that nothing pinned the manifest's bytes.

comparisonProjection.why: 'The two browsers agree cell by cell' is meaningless until it says WHICH fields agree. Timings never match; codes, routes and document effects must.

gestureRule.rule: every caret in every phase is formed the product's way: a click, polled until the engine acknowledges it AND the caret's line box overlaps the target's by more than half the caret's height
gestureRule.why: SPEC E2-C 9.5.6 measured that the gesture changes the engine's own classification, and the first round drove 27 cells with a zero-width selectRange the product never uses. Finding 048 then measured that the click needs 22-28 ms to land, so 'the call returned' is not 'the caret moved'.
gestureRule.acceptance: measured line-box overlap, never a twips constant
gestureRule.acceptanceWhy: 2026-08-16, D3's corpus half: a 195-twip constant (half the LIST corpus's line pitch) refused three cells whose anchors are headings with a 520-twip line box -- the right line, refused by a rule calibrated on a different document, identically in both browsers.

structureComparison.rule: every structural criterion compares the saved document against a NO-ACTION CONTROL save of the same document, never against the fixture on disk
structureComparison.why: 2026-08-16: l4-stress-100 carries 100 as-char draw:frame directly under office:text, and BOTH LibreOffice builds drop all of them on a plain ODT-to-ODT convert with no editing at all. Compared against the fixture, every cell touching that document reports content loss caused by an edit that did not cause it. L6 learned the same thing at a smaller size.

thresholds.wasmHeapMeasurementWhy: 2026-08-16, D4: no product path reports a WASM heap size -- sdk-worker.js does not, R7-D's page has published a null for it since it was written, Chrome's measureUserAgentSpecificMemory breakdown has no WASM attribution and Firefox lacks the API. Without the engine field d4-memory is PARTIAL again, by construction.
thresholds.browserPssAbsoluteGrowthNote: Deliberately not a threshold. The first round's PREDICTION added one and Firefox exceeded it (+35.1 MB) while passing the slope (7.52 of 8). Either write it as a criterion here, before running, or do not score it -- what must not happen again is a prediction carrying a clause the matrix does not.

cells.strengthenedCriterion: ONE REVISION ADVANCE PER COMMIT the oracle names, not merely 'the revision moved'. Round 5 (2026-08-16) passed the round-one analyzer while the product silently dropped two of three real commits (finding 050): the analyzer asked whether the revision moved at all, and it had -- for the first commit. A criterion that cannot see two thirds of a user's typing disappear is not measuring the thing the oracle names.

cells.oracle: pressing the PRODUCT PAGE's own save button yields bytes that begin with the ZIP magic PK\u0003\u0004 and open as an ODT; the product's own toast reports a size in KB rather than NaN
cells.why: Added 2026-08-16 after finding 049: the save button had been writing 15 bytes of '[object Object]' since before round one, and no automated round could see it -- every harness calls session.save() itself and destructures {bytes}, so they all exercised the shell's save and never the button. The lesson generalises past this bug: where the harness's path and the user's path differ, only the user's path is unmeasured.

decisionPolicy.why: A manifest-declared action or gesture that fails cannot be narrowed without editing the frozen manifest, and editing it detaches E2-B's 132 runs. So there is no PARTIAL for contract cells -- only for what was declared outside the contract before the round started.

validatorSelfTest.why: SPEC E2-C 9.1. Testing that the validator notices a changed hash is far weaker than the verdict it issues; every predicate that can turn the verdict has to be shown to go red.
